claims: The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of San Diego, California.
The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down on Friday, April 10, 2026.
The Artemis II Orion capsule splashed down at 8:07 p.m. EDT.
The splashdown marked the end of a 10-day crewed lunar mission.
The Artemis II Orion capsule used a multi-stage parachute system to slow its descent to approximately 20 mph after re-entering Earth’s atmosphere.
The Artemis II mission lasted approximately 10 days.
The Artemis II crew splashed down after a trip around the Moon.
The Artemis II Orion capsule hit the atmosphere at nearly 24,000 mph before employing its heat shield and parachutes.
NASA and US Navy teams recovered the four astronauts via helicopter to the USS John P. Murtha.
Russian Soyuz capsules land on land.
American capsules like Orion and SpaceX Crew Dragon use water-based splashdowns.
Heat shields and parachutes survive high temperatures of 5,000°F or higher.
